# Ma'at Project Guide

<!-- Generated by maat agent-setup. Edit carefully; keep human gates intact. -->

Ma'at is the project control plane for Specification and Verification Driven Development. It turns requirements into scoped tasks, enforces allowed files, captures proof, checks quality, and protects human gates.

Required Ma'at version: `maat-v2.2.0-agent-ready`.

Use `maat` from PATH when available. If it is not available, ask the user for the absolute path to `maat.exe`. This generated file intentionally avoids hardcoding a local tool path by default.

## Core Rules

- Ma'at controls edits through the active task.
- The active task scope is the only edit authority.
- SRS and policy outrank task prompts, approved lessons, and memory.
- `.maat` runtime files are control-plane state; do not edit them manually.
- Human gates are proposal-only for agents.

## Roadmap vs Ad-hoc Work

- For imported SRS roadmap work, use `maat start-next` or `maat start REQ-ID`.
- For scoped ad-hoc work, use `maat prepare "specific intent"` or `maat auto "specific intent"`.
- Do not ask Ma'at to auto-implement a vague phase or roadmap item.

## Useful Commands

- `maat bootstrap`: session contract for agents
- `maat status`: current state and next action
- `maat agent-prompt TASK-ID --role builder`: scoped task instructions
- `maat context explain TASK-ID --budget`: context budget and selection explanation
- `maat auto-verify TASK-ID --dry-run`: preview proof pipeline
- `maat auto-verify TASK-ID`: run proof, quality, submit, and policy-check
- `maat why TASK-ID`: latest blocker root cause
- `maat repair TASK-ID`: exact repair checklist
- `maat doctor --artifacts TASK-ID`: stale task-facing artifact diagnostics
- `maat git-doctor`: Git sharing and provenance hygiene
- `maat git-setup`: recommended .gitignore and .maatignore rules

## Human Gates

Agents must not run accept, approve-plan, waive, learn approve/reject/sunset, or task redo confirm commands. They may only propose these commands for a human.

## Supervised Auto

Supervised-auto may approve only policy-bounded safe gates and records decisions in Ma'at events. It does not waive quality, mutate policy, approve lessons, perform destructive git, or replace human acceptance for high-risk architecture work.

## Git Sharing Model

Commit shared Ma'at project rules. Never commit Ma'at runtime state such as tasks, attempts, events, locks, compiled context, reports, snapshots, or evidence. Run `maat git-doctor` before staging shared Ma'at files.

## Help

Run `maat --help` for the command list and `maat COMMAND --help` when supported.
